title: Visualizing DNA replication by single-molecule analysis of replicated DNA
protocol: Ensure that cells are in their exponential growth phase before the experiment.
Pulse cells with 30 μM IdU (final concentration in the media) for 4 hours.
Wash cells with PBS to remove IdU.
Pulse cells with 70 μM CldU (final concentration in the media) for 4 hours.
Spin down suspension cells after the first pulse and wash with 1x PBS before the second pulse.
Prepare 1% low melting agarose gel in 1x PBS and boil the solution for 10 minutes.
Equilibrate the agarose solution to 50°C in a water bath.
Pre-cool 1x PBS buffer and plug mold on ice for 30 minutes.
After the second pulse, detach cells from the culture surface.
Spin down cells and wash with 1x PBS.
Count the cells using yellow light.
Resuspend the cells in ice-cold 1x PBS to a final concentration of 3 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Equilibrate the cell suspension to 42°C in a water bath for 5 minutes.
Add an equal volume of agarose solution to the cell suspension and mix by pipetting up and down.
Place the mixture back into the 42°C water bath for 1 minute.
Pipette the mixture into plug molds (∼80 μL per well for Bio-Rad molds).
Leave the plugs on ice for 20 minutes to solidify.
Remove the plugs from the molds and place them into lysis buffer (0.5 M EDTA + 1% sarcosine).
Add 0.5 mL of proteinase K stock solution (20 mg/mL) per 50 mL of lysis buffer.
Incubate in a 50°C water bath for 14–18 hours.
Change the lysis buffer by carefully pouring off the liquid, ensuring the plugs remain at the bottom.
Add fresh proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to the new lysis buffer and incubate at 50°C for 24 hours.
Repeat the lysis step if necessary.
Wash the plugs with TE (pH 8) for 1 hour at room temperature, rotating on a rocker set to 24 rpm with a 30-degree tilt angle.
Incubate the plugs in fresh TE (pH 8) at 50°C for 1 hour.
Discard buffer.
Incubate the plugs in TE 8 buffer + PMSF at 50°C for 30 min.
Wash the plugs in TE 8 buffer twice at room temperature for 1 hour, rotating.
Add fresh TE 8 buffer and leave at 4°C for 14–18 hours.
Transfer plugs to storage buffer (50 mM EDTA + 10 mM Tris-HCl 8.0) the next day.
Leave plugs in storage buffer at 4°C for 14–18 hours.
Transfer plugs into fresh storage buffer and continue storing the cell plugs at 4°C.
Wash the plugs with 50 mL TE 8 buffer twice for 1 hour at room temperature, rotating.
Quickly rinse the plugs with water; then with Pre-digestion buffer (10 mM MgCl2 + 10 mM Tris-HCl 8.0).
Wash the plugs with 50 mL Pre-digestion buffer at room temperature for 1 hour, rotating.
Repeat step of washing with Pre-digestion buffer twice.
Transfer each plug to a separate 1.5 mL tube.
Equilibrate each plug in 1 mL digestion buffer containing enzyme (NEB buffer with 2X BSA and 4 μL/mL of 100 mM spermidine).
Use GCK or any other program to choose the enzyme and predict DNA fragment size between 100 to 400 kb that contains the region of interest.
Wash with digestion buffer a second time for 30 minutes at room temperature, rotating.
Add 150 μL digestion buffer per plug with 30 units of enzyme.
Pipette up and down to mix solution carefully without touching the cell plug.
Leave the plug on ice for 30 minutes to allow the enzyme to diffuse into the plug.
Incubate for 14–18 hours at the temperature required for each enzyme.
Remove digestion buffer by carefully pipetting.
Rinse plugs with TE 8 first and then wash the plugs with TE 8 for 1 hour at room temperature, rotating.
Wash plugs for several hours with TE 8 on ice or leave them overnight at 4°C.
Dissolve low melting agarose in 0.5x TBE using a microwave.
Let the solution cool to room temperature before casting the gel.
Keep the remaining melted agarose in a 65°C water bath.
Cast a 0.7% agarose gel and let it solidify for at least 1.5 hours.
Pre-cool 3 L of 0.5x TBE in the PFGE apparatus for 1 hour before the run.
Set circulation to 60–70 during the run.
Maintain a temperature inside the apparatus around 12°C during the run.
Remove a 1–3 cm strip from the top of the gel.
Place plugs and markers in horizontal position at the edge of the gel.
Pour remaining agarose to fill the gap and solidify the plugs to the gel.
Pre-cool the gel inside the tank for 10–30 minutes before starting the run.
Set up the PFGE program with parameters depending on the size of the DNA fragment needed.
After the PFGE run, remove the gel.
Cut the gel region containing the DNA as pictured in Figure 1.
Use a ruler to determine the position of the DNA fragments based on the size of the DNA segment of interest.
Set aside the gel with the DNA.
Fill the rest with 1% agarose (SeaKem).
Stain the gel with ethidium bromide at about 0.5 μg/mL for approximately 2 hours, shaking gently.
Cut a 0.5 cm DNA fragment containing the region of interest out of the gel strip using a ruler.
Cut approximately 1-2 mm slivers from both ends of the gel piece for PCR and keep the rest in storage buffer.
Wash the gel slices in agarose digestion buffer (TE 8 + 100 mM NaCl + 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol) for at least 2 hours.
Transfer gel slices to a 1.5 mL tube and add 150 μL of agarase digestion buffer.
Melt the mixture at 72°C for 20 minutes, then equilibrate the solution at 45°C for 1 minute.
Add 1.5 μL of agarase slowly in circular motion on the surface of the solution and mix by rotating the tube gently with your hands for 1-2 minutes.
Digest the agarose at 45°C for 1.5 hours without vortexing or pipetting.
Set up PCR reactions for 6-7 DNA samples surrounding the region likely to contain the DNA of interest based on the marker.
Use 1-2 μL of the melted DNA solution for each PCR reaction.
Design primers specific to your region of interest using NCBI-BLAST.
Soak slides in 1% SDS for at least 1 hour.
Wash the slides with 1% SDS solution followed by rinsing with hot water and a final wash with distilled water.
Immerse the slides in HNO3: HCl (2:1) solution for 14–18 hours in a chemical hood.
Remove the slides from the acid and transfer to a trough of distilled water.
Wash the slides in distilled water three times, each for 3 minutes.
Drain excess water from the slides on a paper towel.
Rinse the slides in a trough of methanol, moving up and down.
Wash the slides in methanol containing amino silane (2 mL stock of amino silane in 500 mL methanol) for 1 hour, shaking constantly at 70 rpm.
Rinse off excess Amino Silane using Methanol.
Wash slides in distilled water three times, each for three minutes.
Rinse slides in 95% Ethanol twice.
Air dry slides with filtered air from a hose.
Place the slides in a desiccator for one to two days.
Carry out a standard midi or maxi prep to obtain DNA.
Perform biotin-nick translation of fosmid DNA using the Invitrogen kit.
Cut ∼1–2 mm slivers from both ends of the gel slice containing the region of interest.
Wash gel slices in 50 mL agarase digestion buffer and equilibrate for at least 2 h, rotating.
Transfer gel slices into a 1.5 mL tube and add 150 μL agarase digestion buffer.
Melt gel slices at 72°C for 20 min.
Equilibrate the tube at 45°C for 1 min.
Add 1.5 μL agarase slowly in circular motion on the surface, mix by rotating the tube gently with your hands for 1–2 min.
Digest the agarose at 45°C for 4 h.
After digestion, add 0.2 μL YOYO to the DNA slowly in a circular motion and incubate for 30 min.
Prepare the humid chamber by placing two moistened kimwipes inside a black slide box and place box in the 37°C room.
Prepare methanol + 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol buffer.
Prepare Denaturation Buffer: 0.1 N NaOH in 70% ethanol + 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol.
Prepare fixation buffer by adding glutaraldehyde to denaturation buffer just before use in the chemical hood.
Clean coverslips with ethanol or methanol just before use.
Place a 22 × 22 mm coverslip at the center of the slide.
Mark denaturation times and cell line names on slides.
Extract 3.5–4 μL of YOYO-stained DNA gently using a pipette tip.
Pipet out DNA solution slowly from one side of the coverslip to allow liquid movement by capillary action under the coverslip.
Mark the position of the coverslip with a diamond glass marker.
Remove the coverslip gently with a razor blade.
Dip slides into Methanol + 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol buffer.
Keep slides in Methanol buffer for at least 10 min before denaturation.
Denature the slides with Denaturation buffer for 8 min.
Denature the slides with Denaturation buffer for 12 min.
Denature the slides with Denaturation buffer for 16 min.
Add glutaraldehyde to Fixation buffer and fix the slides for 5 min.
Wash the slides with 70% ethanol for 1–2 min.
Repeat washing the slides with 70% ethanol for 1–2 min.
Wash the slides with 95% ethanol for 1–2 min.
Wash the slides with 100% ethanol for 1–2 min.
Place the slides in Methanol + 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol jars for 60 min.
Turn on the dry heating block and adjust to 95°C to denature probes.
Prepare the hybridization master mix containing specified components.
Mix the hybridization master mix for at least 30 min in a rotator.
Start preparing the hybridization-probe mixture by adding biotinylated probe to hybridization mixture.
Dry the slides gently with kimwipes on the back and side.
Assemble the hybridization compartment by placing one 22 × 40 mm coverslip over two 11 × 22 mm coverslips.
Place one 11 × 22 mm coverslip onto each side of the positions outside the stenciled area containing stretched DNA.
Position the 11 × 22 mm coverslips over the diamond glass marker stenciled regions to ensure enough space for hybridization compartment formation.
Add hybridization buffer (∼2 μL) onto the two 11 × 22 mm coverslips.
Place one 22 × 40 mm coverslip onto the two 11 × 22 mm coverslips to form a compartment for hybridization with the probe.
Denature the probe at 95°C for 5 min.
Pipette the denatured probe into the compartment.
Place the slides in the humid chamber.
Incubate the slides at 37°C in the humid chamber for 14–18 h.
Prepare post-hybridization wash buffers in ddH2O as specified.
Mix 4x SSC + 40% formamide for two Coplin jars, each containing 125 mL.
Prewarm the 4x SSC + 40% formamide buffer in a 45°C water bath for 1 hour.
Remove coverslip from slide using a razor.
Rinse slides sequentially in two jars of 2x SSC + 1% SDS.
Transfer five slides at a time to the prewarmed 4x SSC + 40% formamide buffer.
Incubate slides in 4x SSC + 40% formamide for 5 minutes.
Next, rinse slides with 2x SSC + 0.1% IGEPAL at room temperature.
Wash slides sequentially in four jars of 4x SSC + 0.1% IGEPAL for 1 to 10 minutes each time at room temperature.
Rinse the slides in 1x PBS + 0.03% IGEPAL at room temperature.
Wipe solution off with kimwipes on the back, sides, and front outside of the stenciled area without drying the DNA-containing area.
Add 20 μL blocking buffer onto a 22 × 30 coverslip.
Incubate slides in the humid chamber at room temperature for 1 hour or longer.
Prepare detection mixture 1 by diluting Avidin Alexa Fluor 350 conjugate antibody (1:15) with blocking buffer, making enough for two uses.
Prepare detection mixture 2 by diluting Biotinylated Anti-Avidin (BAA) antibody (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute Biotinylated Anti-Avidin (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute mouse-anti-IdU (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute rat-anti-CldU (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute Avidin Alexa Fluor 350 conjugate antibody (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute Goat anti-Rat IgG Secondary Antibody Alexa Fluor 488 (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Dilute Goat anti-Mouse IgG Secondary Antibody, Alexa Fluor 568 (1:15) with blocking buffer.
Add 15 μL of the first detection mixture to each slide via a cover slip.
Incubate in the humid chamber at room temperature for 20 min.
Rinse off the coverslips in a jar containing 1x PBS + 0.03% IGEPAL.
Wash the coverslips again with 1x PBS + 0.03% IGEPAL CA-630.
Drain and wipe off liquid from the back, sides, and front of the stenciled area on the slide.
Add 15 μL of the second detection mixture to each slide.
Incubate in the humid chamber at room temperature for 20 min.
Repeat wash step.
Add 15 μL of the third detection mixture to each slide.
Incubate in the humid chamber at room temperature for 20 min.
Repeat wash step.
Add 15 μL of the fourth detection mixture to each slide.
Incubate in the humid chamber at room temperature for 1 hour.
Repeat wash step.
Note: Longer than 1-hour incubation with the fourth detection mixture can cause high background.
Seal the slides with a drop of ProLong Gold Molecular Probe using a 22 × 30 mm coverslip.
Keep the slides at room temperature for 14–18 hours to dry completely before imaging.
Optional: Check the slides on the same day after allowing ProLong Gold to set for at least 1 hour.
